title: Pad See Ew
subtitle: Thai stir-fried wide rice noodles with chicken, egg, and dark soy
excerpt: Pad see ew is a street-food staple across Thailand. Wide rice noodles char slightly against a very hot wok, giving the dish its signature smoky edge. Speed is the key: have everything ready before the heat goes on.
sourceNotes: Pad see ew translates as 'fried with soy sauce'. It is a Chinese-influenced Thai dish, popular as a quick lunch or dinner from market stalls.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soak the noodles up to 1 hour ahead. Mix the sauce in a small bowl so it is ready to pour.

content.text: Cook this in two or three batches if your wok is small. Crowding the wok drops the temperature and steams the noodles instead of charring them.

items.prepNote: wide flat noodles, soaked in cold water for 30 minutes and drained

content.text: Mix together the dark soy, light soy, oyster sauce, and fish sauce in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat the wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add 2 tablespoons of oil.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through and lightly coloured. Push to the side of the wok.
Add the remaining oil and the garlic. Fry for 30 seconds. Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble loosely for 1 minute.
Add the drained noodles and pour the sauce over. Toss everything together. Leave undisturbed for 30 seconds to let the noodles char slightly.
Add the pak choi. Toss for another 1 to 2 minutes until the leaves wilt. Taste and adjust with more fish sauce or soy if needed.
Serve immediately, while the noodles are still hot and slightly smoky.

items.symptom: The noodles are clumping together in the wok.
items.cause: They were not soaked long enough or not drained well.
items.fix: Separate noodles with tongs immediately after adding to wok.

items.cause: The sauce needs more fish sauce or soy.
items.fix: Add fish sauce 1 teaspoon at a time and taste as you go.

items.cause: They soaked too long and became overly soft before cooking.
items.fix: Soak in cold water only; use lukewarm water next time to speed it up.
